claims.text: The balance between configurational entropy and specific enthalpic interactions governs structural and chemical stability in high-entropy alloys.
High configurational entropy generally stabilizes a disordered solid-solution arrangement as temperature increases.
Favorable ordering enthalpy can overcome configurational-entropy stabilization.
Applied compression at elevated temperature promotes atomic rearrangements in Al0.1CrCoFeNi.
Compression-induced atomic rearrangements produce increased short-range chemical order or clustering relative to tensile or unloaded samples.
Al-Ni is a specific favorable atomic pair responsible for the proposed clustering.
Compression accelerates atomic rearrangements rather than merely changing their final configuration.
Increased short-range ordering locally reduces entropy stabilization.
Compression-induced ordering leads to a more chemically inhomogeneous microstructure that may affect high-temperature stability.
AlxCrCoFeNi exhibits substantial chemical clustering over a wide temperature range when x is below 0.5.
The ordering effect is limited to an intermediate temperature window in which mobility is sufficient but thermal agitation does not overwhelm clustering.
The unstressed, annealed Al0.1CrCoFeNi baseline will be a statistically random, single-phase solid solution with minimal short-range order.
Compression-induced ordering will cause measurable X-ray diffraction peak shifts, broadening, or splitting.
Compression-induced ordering will alter pair-distribution-function profiles and produce locally observable clustering in transmission electron microscopy.
Surface-energy effects in nanoalloys may alter the magnitude of ordering and its effect on stability.

Failure to observe a statistically significant increase in ordering or clustering under compression relative to tensile and unloaded controls would falsify the proposed stress-triggered ordering mechanism.

contradictions.description: The material is called equiatomic while the example Al0.1CrCoFeNi is not equiatomic: normalizing the formula gives approximately 2.44 at.% Al and 24.39 at.% each of Cr, Co, Fe, and Ni.
